items.title: Alphabet shares record their worst day ever, shedding $500 billion in value
items.content:
Part of the reason Google's ad revenues from search underperformed is Google’s own “AI Mode” search feature, which results in fewer ads, a top executive told investors. David Paul Morris / Bloomberg via Getty

Oct. 29, 2026, 11:06 AM EDT  /  Updated   Oct. 29, 2026, 4:33 PM EDT

Shares of Google parent company Alphabet sank Thursday by 12.6%, marking the stock’s worst one-day drop ever and wiping out $500 billion in market value.

Alphabet is America’s fourth-largest company, worth $3.47 trillion.

The market value it shed in Thursday’s trading session ranks as the second-worst one-day wipeout in U.S. market history, trailing only Nvidia’s $589 billion drop in late January 2025 .

It was also the latest sign of broader anxiety across Wall Street over how long it will take big artificial intelligence companies to see consistent returns on investments worth hundreds of billions of dollars.

Late Thursday afternoon, Amazon’s stock appeared to be on track to meet a similar fate. The company reported third-quarter revenue after the bell that fell short of Wall Street’s expectations. Its shares quickly slid by 10% in after-hours trading.

Alphabet had reported its latest quarterly financial results Wednesday , revealing that revenues were less than had been anticipated and surprising investors.

It also reported lackluster advertising sales.

items.title: Creating Dynamic Social Media Cards for User Content
items.content:
What should you put on a dynamic custom social media card image?

By “dynamic” social media cards, I mean cards for pages of user-generated content or something like an e-commerce site with loads of different products. Meaning too many pages to reasonably design a custom graphic by hand for each. So what we’re talking about here is a system to generate dynamic images with dynamic data.

If you can custom design a social media card image, you probably should. Make it branded, enticing, and quickly communicate the most important thing about what’s going on at that URL.

A custom-designed card for a specific URL gives you full control. I like Dia’s here: eye-catching imagery, clear branding, and non-duplicative text that tells you exactly what it is.

GitHub is a good example of dynamically generated social media cards. Each repo has a generated image like this:

That’s an image , not a screenshot I took, but one they dynamically created.

A typical implementation makes that show up with meta tags in the HTML response like this:

< meta property = "og:image" content = "https://example.com/images/social/1.jpg" >

< meta name = "twitter:image" content = "https://example.com/images/social/1.jpg" >

< meta name = "twitter:card" content = "summary_large_image" > Code language: HTML, XML ( xml )

There are more possible tags (see the Open Graph protocol ), plus variations and platform-specific stuff, naturally. Plus, typically a site will have other tags that ultimately help with social sharing, SEO, and general UX, like:

< meta name = "description" content = "A cool demo of a raccoon in roller skates." >

< link rel = "icon" type = "image/x-icon" href = "/assets/favicon.ico" /> Code language: HTML, XML ( xml )

An example of a more “complete” set of HTML: < title > Balatro Planet Card Scaling </ title >

< meta name = "description" content = "A code demo by Chris Coyier created on CodePen" >

< link rel = "icon" type = "image/x-icon" href = "/assets/favicon.ico" />

< meta property = "og:title" content = "Balatro Planet Card Scaling" > < meta property = "og:description" content = "Interactive Example of the +Mult and +Chips scaling of Planet Cards in the game Balatro" >

< meta property = "og:url" content = "https://codepen.io/editor/chriscoyier/pen/01a14173-dbcb-7828-afc4-9a8907157ecb" >

< meta property = "og:site_name" content = "CodePen" >

< meta property = "og:image" content = "https://codepen.io/screenshots/xxx/1280.jpg" >

< meta property = "og:image:width" content = "1280" >

< meta property = "og:image:height" content = "720" >

< meta name = "twitter:card" content = "summary_large_image" >

< meta name = "twitter:site" content = "@CodePen" >

< meta name = "twitter:creator" content = "Chris Coyier " >

< meta name = "twitter:title" content = "Balatro Planet Card Scaling" >

< meta name = "twitter:description" content = "Interactive Example of the +Mult and +Chips scaling of Planet Cards in the game Balatro" >

< meta name = "twitter:image" content = "https://codepen.io/screenshots/xxx/1280.jpg" > Code language: HTML, XML ( xml )

I’m pretty sure you still use the twitter:foo meta tags for X, if you care to. The “X” docs have no guidance on this. Should they just support og:foo style tags? Yes. Do they? I don’t think so, but please correct me if I’m wrong.

Also weird: I used GitHub as an example above, but many of the meta/og tags don’t appear in the GitHub HTML source when you view a repo, so they must do something extra exotic to make it happen. 🤷‍♀️

With those tags in place, supporting platforms will show special extra content. For example, if I text this repo to someone over iMessage, this is what they see:

iMessage is one of the few where the actual URL is hidden and replaced by the unfurl.

This is referred to as unfurling . How a link unfurls .

items.summary_ko: 페이지가 너무 많아 일일이 디자인하기 어려운 사용자 생성 콘텐츠나 상품이 많은 이커머스 사이트를 위해, 동적 데이터로 소셜 미디어 카드 이미지를 자동 생성하는 방법을 다룬다. 가능하면 맞춤 디자인을 권하며, 브랜드가 드러나고 눈길을 끌며 해당 URL의 핵심을 한눈에 전달해야 한다고 강조한다.
items.content_ko: 저자는 페이지 수가 많아 일일이 디자인할 수 없는 경우를 '동적' 카드로 정의한다. 가능하다면 맞춤 디자인을 하는 것이 좋으며, 브랜드를 살리고 눈길을 끌며 URL의 핵심을 빠르게 전달해야 한다고 조언한다. 예로 Dia의 카드를 들어, 눈길을 끄는 이미지, 뚜렷한 브랜드, 중복되지 않는 텍스트를 강점으로 꼽는다. GitHub가 저장소마다 이미지를 동적으로 생성하는 방식도 소개한다. 일반적인 구현은 HTML 응답에 og:image, twitter:image 메타 태그를 넣어 이미지를 지정하는 것이다. (원문이 중간에 끊겨 있음)

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

개별 이미지들의 위치 변경, 삭제, 별칭 추가, 폴더명 변경을 할 수 있습니다

Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk) Built for Coders, Trusted by Defenders.

Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk) Built for Coders, Trusted by Defenders.

Mistral released Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk), a 1-trillion-parameter multimodal model, now available with improved coding, cybersecurity, and reasoning efficiency. It leads open-weight benchmarks in coding and defensive security while offering three reasoning modes for cost-performance balance. Fully open-weight and European-trained, it empowers sovereign AI with customizable, self-hosted deployment options.

We release the weights of Le Chonk, advancing the frontier of open models in agentic coding and cybersecurity.

Earlier this month, we released Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk), our flagship 1-trillion-parameter, natively multimodal model, in public preview. The response to the preview has exceeded our expectations, and we're grateful to our developer community, early-access customers, and partners for their support, collaboration, and feedback.

Since then, we've put that feedback to work while continuing to scale reinforcement learning, driving massive improvements in coding and defensive cybersecurity . Gains continue to accelerate, with no signs of saturation.

Today, we're releasing the weights of this improved Mistral Large 4. The new model also features substantial gains in reasoning efficiency that give developers greater performance while lowering inference costs.

Mistral Large 4 ranks as the best open-weight model for coding and among the world's most capable open models overall. Trained from scratch on European infrastructure with clear lineage from inception to release, it gives organizations a trusted foundation for Sovereign AI

Mistral is defining the sovereign AI category and leading the open frontier. We're committed to building the world's most capable models and releasing them openly, giving developers, enterprises, and institutions the power to own, customize, and control their AI.

items.title: Incident Report: unsanctioned agent behaviour during cyber testing | AISI Work
items.content:
You can access the full technical report here.

AISI’s role is to evaluate and understand the capabilities of frontier AI models, surfacing potential risks before they reach the public. To assess what these models can do, including whether they could be misused for cyberattacks, we test them under deliberately permissive conditions: with access to the open internet, and with some safety filters disabled.

On 28 th July 2026, AISI's Security Team detected unusual data transfers leaving our research systems during a routine cyber evaluation. On investigation, we found that some of the agents being tested had engaged in sustained, potentially harmful activity directed at real people and organisations. We declared a security incident and, within roughly one hour of discovery, had contained it and begun a full investigation.

The incident stemmed from a single evaluation where agents were given a task of solving a cyber security challenge. We ran this challenge 122 times across several models. Our investigation found that in 10 of those runs, an AI agent took autonomous, unsanctioned action on the live internet, targeting real people and organisations. In total, we catalogued 19 such actions. Almost all of this behaviour (17 actions) came from a single model, Anthropic's Mythos 5, with 2 actions involving OpenAI's GPT-5.6-Sol with cyber classifiers (mechanisms to prevent misuse) disabled. In the most serious case, an agent tried to insert malicious code into an open-source project. In an attempt to get the code approved, the agent engaged in social engineering  — creating fake online identities and using them to pressure the project's maintainer to approve the code. A human maintainer caught and refused to approve the malicious code.

These attempts were unsuccessful, and our investigations have not evidenced any resulting real-world harm. But this is the first time we have seen risks around autonomy and deception manifest this clearly, without specific prompting, in the real-world.

Importantly, this was not a case of a model escaping its secure test environment, or ‘sandbox’. As was standard in our cyber testing, we had intentionally permitted internet access, and model-provider cyber classifiers were deliberately disabled - conditions that do not reflect how frontier models are made available to the public. We do this to best assess the maximum capability of models. These configuration choices have been common practice in frontier AI evaluations. The specific models in question, in the configurations in which we tested them are not commercially available and there is no clear indication of similar activity outside of testing scenarios.

Ahead of publishing this blog, we notified GitHub (the developer platform accessed during the evaluation) of the agents' malicious activity, which included actions that GitHub has confirmed violated their terms of service. We worked together with GitHub to remove artefacts left behind by the agent, and to notify the GitHub users the model interacted with. We have also contacted other affected parties. We also intend to work with METR (Model Evaluation and Threat Research) to conduct an independent third-party review – we are still working through the scope of this review with them.

This incident should be interpreted with caution and nuance. To some degree, our evaluation design choices and specific configurations enabled the behaviour. Nonetheless, the activity undertaken by the agent show signs of novel, potentially deceptive behaviours, and were to an extent and severity we did not anticipate.

There are important caveats to bear in mind: we observed a small number of events under very specific conditions, and cannot yet say how likely such behaviour is in different contexts or outside of testing environments. items.title: Reddit is becoming "a logged-in-only experience"
items.content:
Reddit is making a major change to how users access the platform

Add as a preferred source on Google Follow on Google News

Reddit is preparing to make a major change to how people access the platform, with plans to move toward a primarily logged-in experience after more than 20 years of allowing users to browse without an account.

The change was announced by Reddit CEO Steve Huffman, known online as Spez, who explained that the company wants to improve personalization, protect its data, and deliver more relevant advertisements.

While Reddit has traditionally allowed visitors to browse most of its content without signing in, that experience could soon become more limited as the company begins testing new restrictions.

Reddit explains why it wants users to log in

In an October 29 post titled “About that login screen,” Huffman confirmed that Reddit is moving toward a primarily logged-in platform, citing several reasons behind the decision.

“We’re making the change because it’s better for user experience, better for our ads business, is more in line with safety regulations, and more protective of Reddit data,” he explained.

According to Huffman, Reddit has grown to the point where personalization is increasingly necessary to help users find relevant communities and discussions.

The company also wants more visitors to participate in the platform’s core features, including joining communities, voting on posts, and leaving comments, all of which already require an account.

Another major factor is protecting Reddit’s data from unauthorized collection.

Huffman explained that most unauthorized scraping of Reddit’s content currently happens through its logged-out experience. Requiring users to sign in would give the company greater control over how its data is accessed and used.

Reddit is considering implementing human verification for its users

Reddit CEO unphased by historic Blackout, assures staff it “will pass”

Reddit CEO reveals plans to paywall “new types of subreddits”

The change could also benefit Reddit’s advertising business by allowing it to serve more personalized ads while helping the platform comply with regulations around the world.

However, Huffman emphasized that users will not be required to provide their real names or verify their identities simply to log in.

“We don’t need your name. We don’t need to know who you are. We don’t need to know your identity. Honestly, we don’t want to know,” he said.

Reddit will begin testing login restrictions outside the US

Despite the planned changes, Reddit does not intend to completely eliminate access for people who aren’t signed in.

Huffman acknowledged that allowing visitors to view the front page and access posts shared through search engines or external links remains important.

The company has not yet determined exactly which parts of Reddit will require an account.

Instead, it plans to begin testing the new experience in select markets outside the US over the coming months before deciding how to proceed.

Reddit is also bringing back a redesigned incognito mode in its mobile app, allowing users to browse and search without affecting their account’s activity or personalization.

The feature will be read-only, meaning users won’t be able to interact with posts while using it.

Users will also have the option to disable personalization while logged in, although Huffman warned that doing so could make the platform less useful.

For now, Reddit has not announced a specific date for a broader rollout or confirmed whether the changes will eventually apply to all users worldwide.

items.title: Linux Kernel TCP Flaw With 9.8 CVSS Score Affects Ubuntu, Red Hat and Other Distributions
items.content:
A flaw in the Linux kernel's TCP code, tracked as CVE-2026-98432 , affects Ubuntu, Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL), and other Linux distributions. The kernel's own CVE team rates it 9.8 out of 10 on the CVSS scale.

Anthropic said on October 27 that its AI model wrote an exploit that uses the flaw to let a remote attacker with no credentials run commands as root on Linux servers with a multipath TCP listener.

As of October 29, Ubuntu and RHEL have not released a fixed kernel. Red Hat, Amazon, Oracle, and SUSE score the flaw between 5.9 and 8.1, lower than the kernel team's 9.8.

The flaw is a race condition in the code that sets up new IPv4 TCP connections. It can make the kernel read memory it has already freed, a bug type known as a use-after-free.

The kernel fix credits Anthropic researcher Xinyang Ge with reporting the bug. Neither the CVE record nor the fix mentions multipath TCP (MPTCP). The link between that feature and this bug comes from Anthropic's post.

MPTCP lets one connection use several network paths at once. On Linux, an application must request MPTCP when it opens a socket.

Anthropic's post says the flaw "was patched upstream and backported to all maintained stable kernel branches." For distribution users, that fix arrives only in the vendor's kernel package. Debian, Oracle Linux, SUSE, and Amazon Linux have shipped fixed packages, at least for some of their kernels, but Ubuntu and RHEL have not.

Ubuntu also lists its cloud, FIPS, and real-time kernels as vulnerable or as work in progress. Red Hat says its fixes are "currently deferred to a future update." Neither Red Hat nor Ubuntu gives a release date.

The race happens during the TCP handshake. When a connection is completed, the kernel hands the IP options stored with the pending request to the new socket without copying them.

If that socket is destroyed while another CPU is still using the options to answer a resent connection request, the kernel reads freed memory.

IPv6 is not affected by this race because the kernel copies the options for IPv6 connections.

The bug was introduced in Linux 4.4. Kernel developers applied a fix on October 5, ten days before the CVE was published.

The fix makes the kernel wait until other CPUs finish reading the options before it frees them.

The kernel's CVE team added the 9.8 score to the CVE record on October 24, nine days after publishing the CVE.

Its score assumes an attacker who sends a TCP connection request carrying IPv4 Record Route or Timestamp options, then resends the request to try to win the race. The team rated attack complexity low, saying both sides of the race are "attacker-induced."

In that case, the team says, the bug could send nearby kernel memory back to the attacker, corrupt kernel memory, or crash the system.

As of October 28, the National Vulnerability Database (NVD) had not added its own score and showed the kernel team's 9.8. Ubuntu's page also shows that score.

Red Hat's CVE page rates the flaw Moderate, scoring it 5.9 because the race is hard to win. It says the most likely result is a kernel crash, with memory corruption possible in theory, and that "no confidentiality or integrity impact has been demonstrated."

Red Hat's machine-readable advisory file, updated on October 29, lists the impact as Important and scores the flaw 8.1, with high confidentiality and integrity impact. Red Hat's bug tracker changed the issue's severity from medium to high the same day. On that day, the CVE page showed Moderate and 5.9.

Oracle and SUSE also score the flaw 8.1, with the same CVSS vector as Red Hat's advisory file. Those scores match the kernel team's on every metric except attack complexity, which the vendors rate high and the kernel team rates low. Amazon scores it 7.0.

items.summary_ko: 리눅스 커널 TCP 코드의 결함 CVE-2026-98432가 Ubuntu, RHEL 등 여러 배포판에 영향을 준다. 커널 자체 CVE 팀은 CVSS 9.8로 평가했지만, Red Hat·Amazon·Oracle·SUSE는 5.9~8.1로 평가했다. 10월 29일 기준 Ubuntu와 RHEL은 아직 수정 커널을 내놓지 않았다.
items.content_ko: Anthropic은 10월 27일 자사 AI 모델이 이 결함을 이용하는 익스플로잇을 작성했다고 밝혔다. 이를 통해 자격 증명이 없는 원격 공격자가 멀티패스 TCP(MPTCP) 리스너가 있는 리눅스 서버에서 root 권한으로 명령을 실행할 수 있다고 한다. 결함은 새 IPv4 TCP 연결을 설정하는 코드의 레이스 컨디션으로, 이미 해제된 메모리를 읽는 use-after-free 버그다. 커널 수정 사항은 Anthropic 연구원 Xinyang Ge의 보고를 명시했다. CVE 기록과 수정 내용에는 MPTCP 언급이 없으며, 둘을 잇는 내용은 Anthropic의 게시글에만 있다. MPTCP는 하나의 연결이 여러 네트워크 경로를 동시에 쓰게 하며, 리눅스에서는 애플리케이션이 소켓을 열 때 이를 요청해야 한다. 원문은 상류(upstream)에 패치되었고 유지보수 중인 모든 안정 버전에 백포트되었다고 한다. items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

마치 테러리스트가 인질극 벌이는데 인질 죽는다고 테러리스트 진압 안하겠다는 것과 같은 말이다.

총수, 의장 검찰 총원해서 조져 놓다가 사면을 해놓으니까 버릇이 안좋아 진건지 아니면 반도체좀 했다고 뭐가 된양인지 모르겠다만

앞으로 대한민국에서도 여당과 야당 합작으로 대기업 총수, 의장 사법처리하고 사면하지않고 만기 출소하는 케이스가 단 한 번이라도 나와서 명확하게 그 선례를 남겨놔야한다는게 내 생

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

해킹 문제를 해결하는 Capture The Flag(CTF)을 다루는 갤러리입니다.

items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-119286 📢 Source: GitHub_M 💣 CVSS Score: 0.0 (NA) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: False GraphQL-core is a Python port of the GraphQL.js reference implementation. From 3.3.0a3 until 3.3.1, validate() reuses a module-level ValidationAbortedError when a document exceeds max_errors. Python appends frames to the reused exception's traceback on every raise, retaining each document, validation context, and error set for the process lifetime. An unauthenticated client can repeatedly submit a small document with more than 100 validation errors to cause unbounded memory growth before query execution, eventually exhausting worker memory without disclosing or modifying data. This issue is fixed in version 3.3.1. 📅 Published Date: 2026-10-29T21:38:43.633Z https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-119286

items.summary_ko: Python용 GraphQL 구현체 graphql-core의 3.3.0a3부터 3.3.1 이전 버전에 메모리 증가 취약점 CVE-2026-119286이 있다. 검증 오류가 100개를 넘는 작은 문서를 인증 없이 반복 전송하면 메모리가 계속 늘어 워커 메모리가 고갈될 수 있다. 데이터 노출이나 변조는 없으며, 3.3.1 버전에서 수정되었다.
items.content_ko: 원인: validate()가 max_errors를 넘는 문서를 만나면 모듈 수준의 ValidationAbortedError 예외 객체를 재사용하는데, Python은 raise할 때마다 그 예외의 traceback에 프레임을 덧붙인다. 그 결과 문서, 검증 컨텍스트, 오류 집합이 프로세스가 살아 있는 동안 계속 보관된다. 공격 조건: 인증이 필요 없고, 검증 오류가 100개를 넘는 작은 문서를 반복 제출하면 된다. 영향: 쿼리 실행 전 단계에서 메모리가 무제한 증가해 워커 메모리가 고갈될 수 있다. 수정 버전은 3.3.1이다. CVSS 점수는 0.0(N/A), 원격 악용 가능 여부는 False로 표기되어 있다. 게시 시각은 2026-10-29 21:38(UTC)이다.

items.title: DoorDash to acquire Instacart
items.content:
Transaction values Instacart at $65.00 per share, representing a 26% premium to Instacart's closing price on October 22, 2026

Together, DoorDash and Instacart would help stores of every size reach more customers with the kinds of innovative technology that the biggest online retailers and grocers build for themselves

Consumers to benefit from more choice and access to affordable delivery and savings

Dashers and Shoppers to have more earnings opportunities and more choice over when and how they earn

DoorDash, Inc. (NASDAQ: DASH) and Maplebear Inc. (d.b.a. Instacart, NASDAQ: CART) today announced a definitive agreement under which DoorDash will acquire Instacart for a total value of $65.00 for each Instacart share, or an equity value of approximately $17 billion. The aggregate transaction consideration will be at least 75% cash, with Instacart stockholders able to elect cash, DoorDash stock, or a combination of both, subject to proration so that DoorDash stock does not exceed 25% of the aggregate consideration. Instacart's board of directors has unanimously approved the agreement.

DoorDash and Instacart share a mission to help local businesses succeed. Families turn to Instacart for the big weekly shop and to DoorDash for meals and nearly anything else they need from their neighborhood in under an hour. The combined company will offer grocers and retailers of every size DoorDash's delivery network and Instacart's grocery and fulfillment technology, in both apps and on stores' own websites, along with the advertising and AI tools each company has built. On either app, customers pick a store in their own community, and the store makes the sale. Consumers will have more stores to choose from, more savings opportunities when they choose to shop with a local business, and faster delivery options, while Dashers and Shoppers will have more ways to earn.

Most grocery shopping still happens in stores, but more people are buying groceries and everyday goods online. They expect fast, affordable delivery and an easy way to order. The biggest online retailers and grocers are racing ahead, building their own delivery fleets, warehouses, membership programs, and AI shopping assistants. A grocer or retailer running on thin margins cannot build all of that alone, and with AI, the playing field risks being tilted even further away from local commerce.

DoorDash and Instacart believe that communities benefit when Main Street competes, and they build the tools that empower local businesses. Together, they could help local stores grow online. More grocers could deploy Instacart's technology to run their own websites and retail media networks, bringing them more sales and advertising revenue. Brands would gain a scaled alternative for reaching customers online. Grocers could add capacity for online orders through DoorDash's DashMart Fulfillment Services and offer faster, more accurate, and more affordable delivery.

“Grocery is one of the hardest things to get right online. Someone has to pick a ripe avocado, find a substitute you’d choose yourself, and get the ice cream to you before it melts,” said Tony Xu, co-founder and CEO of DoorDash. “Instacart has spent years learning to do that well for grocers, while DoorDash has built a delivery network and technology that local stores rely on every day. Together, we could give stores of every size more of those tools and unlock the potential of grocery delivery. It’s still early innings, but we know that when more people shop local, more dollars stay local.”

“Over the last 14 years, Instacart has transformed online grocery by helping retailers of all sizes compete and grow, and joining forces with DoorDash allows us to do even more,” said Chris Rogers, CEO of Instacart. “When our purpose-built grocery technology and trusted retailer and brand relationships are combined with DoorDash’s global consumer reach and logistics capabilities, we can create new opportunities for our retail and brand…

items.title: Shared password manager for families?
items.summary: ask, security
items.content:
Long story short, I need to have a bunch of shared accounts with family for finance and insurance and stuff, mostly for the sake of family members who are getting old and need help keeping things organized. So the requirements are:

I would just use 1Password, but recent events have demonstrated them as not exactly competent. I could always use KeepassXC and keep the file in a Google Drive folder, or maybe teach my siblings to use Syncthing, but that feels like extra steps we could do without. Anyone have any recommendations for how to do this well?

If you can selfhost I'd recommend looking at Vaultwarden . They support sharing credentials in groups and emergency access conditions, which have proved useful to me and my family in the past. The apps/integrations (Android, iOS, Browsers, Desktop, CLI) are provided by Bitwarden and they are available cross platform.

That's what I'm using right now, and it's great. I'm not switching away yet, but Bitwarden's recent license changes for their clients have made the hairs on the back of my neck stand up.

So far, it's not a pressing concern for me, but it's made me slightly less eager to recommend my setup to others. I hope they maintain the status quo.

Here's the license change details for those who, like me, missed it: https://community.bitwarden.com/t/published-version-update-in-app-stores/102750/7

Same boat here. So far I'm still happy with my setup but it feels like it's on borrowed time. There may be a point where a community fork is inevitable.

I have my hopes high with things like rbw already out there.

I second vaultwarden, the bitwarden modules are useful & easy to understand (tested on android & firefox).

+1 I use the saas / online version for my family and it has worked well for us.

I host vaultwarden at home reachable via wirguard. Works really great.

I would just use 1Password, but recent events have demonstrated them as not exactly competent.

1password didn't fix clickjacking attack vulnerability (reported in April last year) over 4 months before disclosure (August last year) and it still wasn't fixed in January this year. I didn't take time to check whether it's still the case

That doesn’t seem like a big deal to me.

I'd say any known attack for a password manager is big HUGE, no matter the prerequisites

They also sponsor DHH's Omarchy, which is why I switched to Bitwarden.

Would simply Apple Passwords work? The sharing feature is great

I accepted to migrate my phone/laptop to Apple in order to simplify this type of situation around Apple tools for family, subscriptions and passwords sharing. The last part I am not convinced is regarding mail management. For now, everyone keeps their but I would like to have a shared set-up in the future.

I use KeepassXC with Syncthing for personal and team databases, the only downside of it is merge conflicts, but I'm not really worried about it as it doesn't happen often and syncthing keeps the conflict so i wont lose the data

But the bigger challenge is sharing the second factor ( email token, phone token, passkey , 2fa ). And every app now has a unique process that is constantly changing. You can’t plan ahead of time

If you pay for Bitwarden, you can store TOTP codes in it, at least. If the email credentials are in the vault you can get email tokens too. SMS is the only one that would be troublesome.

Bitwarden supports passkeys and 2fa codes, although I'm not sure what the sharing story looks like for those. That said, I've had trouble getting passkeys to work properly and consistently across browsers and operating systems - on Android and MacOS, the system key management system tends to want to take over, which means resorting back to TOTP.

(I'm not sure which features are free and which are paid for Bitwarden, but passkeys definitely seem to be free, and I think TOTP is as well these days. Plus there's always Vaultwarden which does it all for free if you self host.)

I'm happy with Proton Pass and it should…

items.title: Google Starved Out Publishers With AI Search. Now, Its Pivot Is Blowing Up in Its Face: Its AI Mode isn't the cash cow it hoped it would be.
items.content:
Woe is Google. After it starved out publishers with its AI features, it’s now getting a taste of its own medicine.

Shares of its parent company Alphabet took an over 11 percent nosedive on Wednesday, after it disclosed that its AI search features are raking in less money than its traditional search ad model. The steep correction wiped out more than $500 billion in market value .

In its Q3 report, Google reported a quarterly revenue of $127.6 billion, a 25 percent year over year increase. But it’s also spending more, with capital expenditures more than doubling from last year to $51.4 billion, largely thanks to its massive AI investments.

Meanwhile, the growth of its revenue from search seems to be tapering off. It reported a 12 percent year-over-year increase to $63.3 billion, which is less than the 14.5 percent growth it reported in the same period last year.

That’s despite Google Search fielding more queries than ever. Google chief business officer Philipp Schindler admitted in an earnings call, per Search Engine Land , that this was because of “lower monetization we’re seeing in AI Mode,” its AI-powered search experience that works more like a chatbot instead of showing the traditional ten blue links.

It’s an ironic, but perhaps not unforeseen, downturn for Google. When ChatGPT became global phenomenon in late 2022, questions were soon asked regarding if a shift to using chatbots to obtain information over a traditional search engine would topple Google’s ludicrous advertising empire, which earns the company hundreds of billions of dollars each year .

Google responded by developing its own AI features, including its notoriously unreliable AI Overviews , and prominently integrating them into its search engine. This came at the expense of the websites and publishers that its AI models were pilfering from: users were happy to read error-plagued summaries instead of visiting the websites that contained the original information, depriving these sites of clicks and ad revenues. Despite Google’s repeated claims to the contrary, multiple studies have demonstrated that AI Overviews have destroyed click-through rates .

This has had a disastrous effect on the media landscape, with data compiled by Axios showing that the number of visits to top news sites plummeted from over 70 million visitors a month in July of 2024 — the year that Google launched AI Overviews — to just over 47 million in July of 2026. Media leaders who responded to a Reuters Institute survey are grim about the future , predicting traffic to their websites to fall by nearly half over the next three years amidst this AI-dominated paradigm.

Now, Google is getting a taste of this too, earning less advertising dollars from its AI Mode than from the traditional search that it is so eager to abandon. It seemingly hasn’t considered what comes next after the websites it earns money off of all go out of business.

Chief business officer Schindler, though, was adamant that Google will soon start squeeze more money out of AI Mode.

“On AI Mode, many of these queries are upper funnel queries, allowing us to capture new, high-value commercial intent,” he argued. “In addition, the majority of AI Mode queries are incremental, creating more monetization opportunities over time.”

items.title: My favourite PowerMac is a Nintendo Wii
items.summary: retrocomputing, reversing
items.content:
So today I reached a nice milestone in one of my projects: my work porting classic Mac OS to PowerPC systems with what I affectionately call ArtX chipsets (Nintendo GameCube, Wii, eventually Wii U; the GameCube’s Flipper integrated chipset was very much designed by ArtX as it was effectively finished when ATI acquired the company, and the Wii’s Vegas (and its later revision Bollywood) and Wii U’s Latte are effectively straight successors) reached the desktop for the first time, most likely the first time since the CHRP clone era that someone outside of Apple brought up classic Mac OS on a new system to the desktop. Despite still being nowhere near ready for a public release, I want to talk about the challenges I faced with this project so far.

But first, why port classic Mac OS to this hardware in the first place? I’d already ported NT of course, and during that work I acquired some PowerPC Mac laptops which I also ended up porting NT to, work on one port improved the others and so on. This got me acquainted with the classic Mac OS, and I fell in love with the jank as it were (hacks upon hacks upon hacks going back to the 1980s is something I’d definitely describe as “jank”). Not to mention the m68k part of the TBXI is called “SuperMario”, and was for the entire PowerPC era. I wonder if a developer was a fan in the early 1990s?

Also, for the record: I started this project on 2025-06-22 (when I forked upstream openbios), no kind of coding agent or LLM was used, all coding, reversing and debugging work done by myself. I do these projects for fun and to learn, if I used “AI” it wouldn’t be fun and I wouldn’t learn anything.

Let’s start with the initial boot. “New World” classic Mac OS starts out with a bootloader called the “Trampoline”, which runs on an Open Firmware environment. So I needed to port OpenBIOS. Luckily, around this time Goldfish64 had started his own port of Mac OS X to the Wii, and he’d made an OpenBIOS port that I could use some drivers from, although for various reasons I didn’t just want to use his port directly (which was only targeting Wii/Wii U, I wanted to target GameCube too). I also decided to reuse some existing code to make some driver development easier (specifically the display driver), and thus changed my existing NT ARC firmware loader to load a big endian ELF instead.

I needed some small number of disk drivers for initial bringup, so decided to port my two drivers for devices on the EXI bus (this is just Nintendo and Macronix’s name for SPI), the “SD Gecko” (which is just a straight through adapter for a GameCube memory card slot allowing for SD over SPI), and the “EXI-IDE” (my driver is actually not correct to real hardware, but to my inaccurate emulation in my Dolphin tree allowing for testing under emulator with the low level debugging support that implies).

I wasn’t sure what kind of on-disk format I wanted to use (these drivers on my earlier NT port ran entirely using disk images on a FAT filesystem, due to the requirement for compatibiltiy with existing homebrew loaders that load executables from FAT filesystems, but this would naturally be limited to 4GB images for FAT32, and later versions of classic Mac OS needed more), so for initial testing I just took the “Mac OS ROM” TBXI file and placed it directly on a FAT filesystem as \ppc\bootinfo.txt for OpenBIOS to load it on boot.

So with that I could get the Trampoline running. I decided that I should try and apply as many patches to the image as possible as close to run-time as possible, so mostly untouched existing CD images could be used eventually.

The first issue I had was that the Trampoline makes some assumptions of the physical address space layout that are not true for this system. The physical address of a buffer gets calculated as an invalid address, so I patched that to an address guaranteed to be valid, and also the corresponding code setting up the memory chunk list/page table entries for the kernel.

items.summary_ko: 저자는 GameCube, Wii, Wii U 등 ArtX 계열 칩셋 기기에 PowerPC 기반으로 클래식 Mac OS를 이식하는 프로젝트를 진행 중이다. 이번에 처음으로 데스크톱 화면까지 부팅하는 데 성공했지만, 아직 공개 배포 단계는 멀다고 밝혔다. 저자는 Apple 외부에서 새 시스템에 클래식 Mac OS를 데스크톱까지 올린 것은 CHRP 클론 시절 이후 처음일 가능성이 크다고 본다.

items.title: Nissan says Oracle PeopleSoft break-in may have spilled payroll records, SSNs
items.content:
Nissan says Oracle PeopleSoft break-in may have spilled payroll records, SSNs

Carmaker points finger at an 'unknown' flaw as customer fallout continues

Nissan has joined the growing list of Oracle customers cleaning up after a cyberattack, warning employees that payroll records, bank details, Social Security numbers, and other personal data may have been stolen.

In a filing submitted to the California Attorney General on Friday, Nissan Americas said Oracle had informed it of "a cyber event" involving the personnel records of "hundreds of companies." The automaker said it later learned Nissan had been "specifically targeted" in the attack.

A notification sent to current and former employees, seen by The Register , says the company believes attackers accessed a haul of sensitive info, including contact and banking information; Social Security, Social Insurance, or other national identification numbers; financial and tax records; and dependent and beneficiary details.

Current and former employees in the US, Canada, Mexico, and Brazil may have been affected, although Nissan said it is still working to determine exactly whose information was exposed.

Nissan said it kicked off its incident response plan after learning of the intrusion, brought in outside security specialists, and has been working with Oracle while keeping law enforcement informed. It plans to offer affected individuals credit or dark web monitoring where available.

The company has also put a few extra locks on the payroll office. Employees can now access pay slips or update direct deposit details only from a corporate network or through a secure VPN, while Nissan adds extra identity checks before processing payroll requests.

The accompanying employee FAQ pins the incident on "an unknown vulnerability in Oracle's PeopleSoft software" and says the campaign is affecting "hundreds of companies and institutions." The document offers no clue as to what the vulnerability is, whether Oracle has patched it, or whether the compromised PeopleSoft environment was hosted by Oracle or by Nissan itself.

The disclosure lands just weeks after researchers linked the ShinyHunters extortion crew to a wave of attacks exploiting a PeopleSoft zero-day . More than 100 organizations and roughly 300 PeopleSoft instances were reportedly compromised before Oracle issued mitigation measures, with the gang claiming to have made off with HR, payroll, and other enterprise data.

Weak security means attackers could disable all of a city's public EV chargers

US regulator tells GM to hit the brakes on customer tracking

21K Nissan customers' data stolen in Red Hat raid

Porsche panic in Russia as pricey status symbols forget how to car

Oracle has said little publicly about the reported attacks and didn't respond to The Register's questions, even as organizations have continued to disclose being caught in the fallout.

Nissan has not confirmed that the incidents are connected, though its California filing lists the breach period as May 27 through June 9, broadly aligning with the previously reported timeline.

The carmaker didn't respond to questions about how many current and former employees are affected, when Oracle first notified it of the breach, and whether the compromise was limited to Oracle-managed systems. ®

items.title: US data centers could wipe out 15 years' worth of progress in greenhouse gas emissions, report claims — buildouts could emit as much carbon dioxide as all of Mexico.
items.content:
Concerns have been mounting everywhere about the environmental impact of data centers, with alarms ringing at various environmental think tanks. The Sierra Club, one of the oldest environmental preservation organizations in the U.S., has now put forth an estimate that by 2030, U.S. data center buildouts will be outputting as much carbon dioxide as the entirety of Mexico, pushing back progress on greenhouse gas reduction by 15 years, Bloomberg reports.

Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers

America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the price

GTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this year

Demand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsible

The Club's principal advisor for climate and energy, Jeremy Fusher, puts it plainly: "the numbers continue to sort of boggle our minds." He's referring to an estimate that with the output from pending data center builds, the output from the U.S. power sector is set to put 2.1 billion metric tons of CO2 in the atmosphere by the end of the decade, an uptick of 42% compared to 2025 figures. The researchers' previous estimates were between a quarter and half of the current projections.

An increasing number of countries and states are enacting laws demanding that new data center builds have a large portion of their power generated by green sources. However, those laws rarely apply retroactively, and oftentimes have a phase-in period. Even the Irish law on the matter demanding that new data centers be fed by 80% of renewable power only requires that that happens six years after they're powered up.

In the current AI-driven market, speed of construction is king. Roughly 40% of U.S. data centers are fed by natural gas turbines , and the situation doesn't look like it'll be changing much. It'll likely get worse, as the addition of green sources almost assuredly won't keep up with demand. Much like RAM, GPUs, and storage, turbines were all slurped up by data centers. Their prices have risen by 50%, and production is backlogged for years, with one maker stating it's opening slots for production in 2032 .

Having said all that, Brendan Pierpont from Energy Innovation, another climate-concerned organization, points out that although the current path looks dangerous for the environment, it's hard to make a hard prediction of how the situation will play out. He justifies his position with common data center roadblocks: the availability of turbines, delays in grid connections, and other delay factors.

Truth be told, at this point it's hard to predict how many data centers will actually reach completion, given that requests for permits far exceed available grid capacity across the U.S., and a sizable number of buildouts are encountering strong opposition . Plus, although the AI bubble is still alive and well, concerns started to arise about the economics of hyperscalers, indicating some may go the way of the dodo — and their projects along with them.

items.title: Day 20 - Scripting
items.content:
Today is the final session for the course. Pat yourself on the back if you worked your way through all lessons!

You’ve seen that a continual emphasis for a sysadmin is to automate as much as possible, and also how in Linux the system is very “transparent” - once you know where to look!

Today, on this final session for the course, we’ll cover how to write small programs or “shell scripts” to help manage your system.

When typing at the Linux command-line you’re directly communicating with “the command interpreter”, also known as “the shell”. Normally this shell is bash , so when you string commands together to make a script the result can be called either a ‘“shell script”, or a “bash script”.

Why make a script rather than just typing commands in manually?

It saves typing. Remember when we searched through the logs with a long string of grep , cut and sort commands? If you need to do something like that more than a few times then turning it into a script saves typing - and typos!

Parameters. One script can be used to do several things depending on what parameters you provide

Automation. Pop your script in /etc/cron.daily and it will run each day, or install a symlink to it in the appropriate /etc/rc.d folder and you can have it run each time the system is shut down or booted up.

Write a short script that list the top 3 IP addresses that tried to login into your server

Scripts are just simple text files, but if you set the “execute” permissions on them then the system will look for a special line starting with the two characters “#” and “!” - referred to as the “shebang” (or “crunchbang”) at the top of the file.

Normally anything starting with a “#” character would be treated as a comment, but in the first line and followed by a “!”, it’s interpreted as: “please feed the rest of this to the /bin/bash program, which will interpret it as a script” . All of our scripts will be written in the bash language - the same as you’ve been typing at the command line throughout this course - but scripts can also be written in many other “scripting languages”, so a script in the Perl language might start with #!/usr/bin/perl and one in Python #!/usr/bin/env python3

You’ll write a small script to list out who’s been most recently unsuccessfully trying to login to your server, using the entries in /var/log/auth.log .

Use vim to create a file, attacker , in your home directory with this content:

# attacker - prints out the last failed login attempt

echo "The last failed login attempt came from IP address:"

grep - i "disconnected from" / var / log / auth . log | tail - 1 | cut - d : - f4 | cut - f7 - d " "

Putting comments at the top of the script like this isn’t strictly necessary (the computer ignores them), but it’s a good professional habit to get into.

Now to run this script, you just need to refer to it by name - but the current directory is (deliberately) not in your $PATH, so you need to do this either of two ways:

Once you’re happy with a script, and want to have it easily available, you’ll probably want to move it somewhere on your $PATH - and /usr/local/bin is a normally the appropriate place, so try this:

sudo mv attacker /usr/local/bin/attacker

…and now it will Just Work whenever you type attacker

You can expand this script so that it requires a parameter and prints out some syntax help when you don’t give one. There are a few new tricks in this, so it’s worth studying:

# topattack - list the most persistent attackers

# Ensure "graceful exit" in case the script was sourced.

if [[ ${BASH_SOURCE[0]} != "$0" ]]; then

echo "Don't source this file. Execute it.";

# Display usage hint if the script was executed with no/invalid argument.

if [[ -z "$1" ]] || [[ ! "$1" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || (( $1 < 1 )); then

echo -e "\nUsage:\n\t$(basename "${BASH_SOURCE:-$0}") <NUM>";

echo "Lists the top <NUM> attackers by their IP address.";

echo -e "(<NUM> can only be a natural number)\n";

items.summary_ko: 최종 과정으로 셸 스크립트를 작성해 시스템을 자동화하는 방법을 다룬다. 스크립트는 타이핑 시간을 절약하고 매개변수로 다양한 작업을 수행하며 자동화를 통해 효율성을 높인다.
items.content_ko: Linux 커맨드 라인은 '커맨드 인터프리터' 또는 '셸'과의 직접 통신이다. 보통 bash 셸을 사용하며 명령을 조합한 스크립트를 '셸 스크립트' 또는 '배시 스크립트'라 부른다. 스크립트의 장점은 타이핑 절약(grep, cut, sort 등 긴 명령어 조합 반복 시 효과적), 매개변수를 통한 다양한 작업 수행, 자동화다. 스크립트를 /etc/cron.daily에 넣으면 매일 자동 실행되거나 심링크를 설치하면 정기적으로 실행된다.

items.title: LLM Voice
items.content:
Sometimes when I read a post, I get the growing feeling that I'm reading

the output of an LLM. I can't necessarily define why, although there are the common

tells (it's not the em-dashes, it's the load-bearing tapestries). As I

do this my desire to read on atrophies, sometimes to the point of revulsion

There are tools out there that claim to be able to tell the difference

between LLM-written prose and the old-fashioned biological product. I'm wary

of them, partly due skeptism about their accuracy, but also because it rather

misses the point. The reaction to LLM-Voice is a human one, that sense that we

valley of prose. By the time I'd reach for a tool to tell me what I'm

reading, it's already too late, even if it confidently tells me there's no LLM

I'm also suspicious of my own ability to accurately recognize LLM voice. Language

changes over time, so a common sign of age is complaining about the language

of the youngs. I'm inclined to bristle at prose that talks about “adopting a

new sales motion ,” or “a sharp round-up of news”. But I've heard

these constructs coming out of human mouths, so that's more a generational

difference rather than between carbon and silicon. (And as a transplanted Brit,

don't get me started on Americanisms, I'm sure I'll get used to them momentarily.)

Right now I urge authors to be extra-wary of LLM-Voice. In particular I

strongly recommend that authors should not fall into the trap of getting the

LLM to write a draft. Even if it's edited by a human, it's very hard to expel

the LLM-Voice - thus causing the uncanny valley reaction. 1 Even accepting suggestions of rephrasing is dangerous. I

have heard of people using LLMs to develop outline and structure, that

may be ok, but only as far as an outline. 2

Authors should fill the prose themselves.

Very hard, but not impossible. I've come across one case where I do know

the first draft was entirely done by LLM, but I detected no LLM Voice when

I read the final piece. It did, however, need a professional editor at a

major periodical publication to clean it up.

My policy on this site, is that anyone who uses AI to help them write

should declare how they used it, usually in the

acknowledgments. This is partly for transparency, and partly so that

readers can learn useful ways to use AI. In my own case, I don't use AI

for generating prose, nor for help in structure. The only way I use it for

writing is as a search tool (but I verify any information by going

even more important in the age of LLMs. I habitually speak the words in my head

and then write them down (and then edit what I've just written). This advice

is particularly important to anyone who has any desire to communicate

regularly with writing. Like many things, learning to be a good writer relies

on lots of practice. It's a skill worth the time to acquire, but surrendering

In time it may be that LLMs will be so good that we can't tell the

difference. In many ways, that's more worrying. Like most writers, I find

writing an almost-essential tool for thinking. Often it's only by writing

something down, that I can really get my thoughts on a topic into coherence.

I've often started an essay knowing I don't really understand something, but

the act of wrestling with the words forces me to overcome my confusions. As

more people delegate writing to LLMs they will also delegate thinking and

comprehension to LLMs. I don't want to do that, where's the fun of writing then?

Although avoiding LLM-Voice is a general rule, it isn't an absolute one. An

important example is that of Jim Highsmith (who contributes to this site). He

items.title: Qwenputer: a fully functioning, deterministic RISC-V CPU inside Qwen3.5
items.summary: ai
items.content:
Qwenputer is a pretty fun experimental model. It's a stock Qwen 3.5 4B with one addition: a RISC-V CPU embedded within the weights that uses the model's own Gated DeltaNet attention layers as RAM. (To learn how GDN works, here's a handy guide .) This 'CPU' runs completely within the forward passes of the model, and can run arithmetic operations, C and MicroPython code without any external runtime or tool usage whatsoever.

To be very clear, it is not a plugin, a tool or a sandbox. This blog will explain exactly how this model works, and how the model utilises GDN layers as RAM, and how I also slotted in an experimental in-model file storage.

I also wrote up two follow-ups built on top of Qwenputer: how hybrid models can learn to hide their reasoning in their RNN state and evade CoT monitoring , and how compiled weights like these can work as inbuilt monitoring tools that the model itself can't tamper with .

Qwen hands a multiplication to the RISC-V CPU inside its own weights; the CPU's RAM is Gated DeltaNet state

You can grab Qwenputer from Hugging Face or ModelScope , and the code is on GitHub .

Qwen3-Next and Qwen 3.5 (the model Qwenputer is built on) use a pretty neat trick. 3 out of 4 attention layers in the model use Gated DeltaNet, a linear RNN, as the attention mechanism ( more on that here ). Each head keeps a state matrix, and the delta rule keeps this updated.

Now, here's where our fun experiment starts. I found out that by setting the gate to 1, 1 1 Each Gated DeltaNet head keeps a state matrix, its memory. At every token, before writing anything new, it multiplies the whole state by the gate, a number between 0 and 1. That's how the RNN forgets: a gate of 0.9 fades everything stored a little on every token, and a gate of 1 means nothing ever fades. the write strength (beta) to 1, 2 2 After the gate, the head nudges one direction of the state towards a new value, and the write strength beta sets how far. A beta of 1 means the old value along that direction is replaced completely instead of blended. and using one-hot key encoding, 3 3 A one-hot key is a vector of zeros with a single 1 in it, so it points at exactly one row of the state, the way a memory address points at one cell. every write we perform will overwrite exactly one row, and every one-hot query can retrieve an exact value. This means that the GDN layers themselves can work exactly as RAM, at a far lower cost than using normal attention as RAM, since a GDN head's state stays the same size however long the conversation gets, unlike attention's KV cache.

Gated DeltaNet state used as RAM: a one-hot key overwrites one row, a one-hot query reads it back, and the CPU keeps its registers, memory and program counter in those rows

The idea that the delta rule acts as a memory isn't new: Schlag et al. (2021) showed that linear attention with the delta rule works as an associative memory, or "fast weights". 4 4 Imanol Schlag, Kazuki Irie and Jürgen Schmidhuber, " Linear Transformers Are Secretly Fast Weight Programmers ", ICML 2021. The new thing here is making it exact and addressable, inside a production model, reliably enough to run a whole CPU on it.

This is the base on which this entire model is built. As it stands, default Qwen 3.5 does not keep exact values in the GDN. With this modification, we unlock the next part of this experiment.

Since we have a fully functional, cheap and fast RAM now, we can go ahead with compiling a working CPU into the model weights. Luckily, there's no training involved: a compiler sets every weight directly. You describe the CPU as a circuit, a long list of small steps like "read this register", "add these two numbers" or "jump if zero", and the compiler turns each step into a piece of a transformer layer: attention heads that look things up, feed-forward units that do the arithmetic, and DeltaNet heads that hold the RAM. The CPU then runs as the model decodes.

items.title: Chinese Hackers Abused Google Workspace Rules to Steal Research and Defense Emails
items.content:
A China-linked espionage group hid inside North American medical, academic, and military research networks for more than a year, quietly stealing sensitive research and defense email.

The way in was a backdoor on their REDCap research servers that stole login credentials. The exfiltration was the unusual part: the attackers rewired the victims' own Google Workspace rules to copy any message matching their keywords to an inbox they controlled.

Google's Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) laid out the campaign in a report published this week and attributes it with high confidence to a cluster it tracks as UNC6508.

The actor and its REDCap backdoor are not new names; Google first surfaced both in February , in a wider report on state-backed attacks against the defense sector. It did not name the victims, describing them only as multiple organizations across the US and Canada: clinical providers, academic centers, military health institutions, advocacy groups, and health regulators.

Google says it notified them and disrupted the group's infrastructure.

The entry point was REDCap (Research Electronic Data Capture), a web platform that hospitals and universities use to build and manage study databases. UNC6508 compromised externally facing REDCap servers.

Google has not pinned down the initial access vector, named a specific CVE, or listed the affected versions, though it saw the group probing older, vulnerable ones.

Around three months after getting in, the group deployed custom malware GTIG calls INFINITERED , which trojanizes REDCap's own system files and does three things.

The earliest known compromise dates to September 2023, with activity continuing through November 2025. Once on the server, UNC6508 ran internal reconnaissance and credential discovery, pulling database and service account credentials, then used those logins to move into the internal network and on to a domain administrator account.

Google does not spell out the exact path to that admin account. With admin rights, the group set up the exfiltration.

The exfiltration rode a feature that was already there. UNC6508 abused content compliance rules, a legitimate Google Workspace admin feature that scans mail for keywords and can copy or forward matching messages.

Similar features exist in other cloud mail suites. The group created a rule, misspelled "Patroit," that watched for nearly 150 keywords, search terms, and email addresses. When a message matched, Workspace silently BCC'd it to an attacker-controlled Gmail address, which Google has since disabled. No malware on the mail server, no separate exfiltration tool, no unusual network traffic. Just a built-in mail feature, turned to copy the organization's secrets to an inbox the attackers owned.

MITRE already catalogs email-forwarding-rule abuse as a known technique. What GTIG flags as new here is the use of domain content compliance rules to do it, a method it says it had not seen from a China-linked actor before.

The rule's keywords mapped to UNC6508's collection priorities: geo-strategic policy, military strategy and equipment, advanced technology including AI and uncrewed vehicles, offensive cyber programs, and medical research. One term stood out for its specificity, chikungunya , the mosquito-borne virus behind a 2025 outbreak in China's Guangdong province.

Start with REDCap. Patch externally facing servers and remove old versions outright, not just alongside the current build. REDCap lets legacy versions run side-by-side, and that is what enables downgrade attacks, where an attacker forces software back to a known-vulnerable release.

Then check the mail side. Review Workspace, or equivalent, content compliance and mail-forwarding rules for anything that BCCs or reroutes mail to outside addresses. Check admin audit logs for when rules changed, not just what they say now. Pull GTIG's published indicators and hunt for INFINITERED. items.title: Man granted first-of-its-kind religious exemption against mandatory AI use at work
items.content:
David Durman, a research administrator at the University of Kentucky (UK), has successfully argued that using AI violates his beliefs as a humanist and has received Title VII religious accommodation from university officials not to use the technology. According to the Religion News Service (RNS) , Durman believes in "the human part of life," which includes making his own decisions. However, he says that when the UK asked its employees to use AI, he felt that doing so would mean outsourcing his thinking to tools like ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot, thus violating his deeply held beliefs.

“The process and work involved in thinking through situations, through my work, through my ethics, through the way I handle other people, is a key component in being able to develop myself as a moral person,” Durman told RNS in an interview. “And offloading that labor, regardless of whether it’s taxing or not, is undercutting my ability to be a moral actor.” Because of this, the research administrator was granted a Title VII exemption under the Civil Rights Act of 1964, which prohibited employment discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, and national origin. While humanism is often a non-religious philosophy or a worldview, federal courts have ruled that it qualifies as a religion.

The American Humanist Association (AHA) assisted Durman with his request for the accommodation. “This is the first of its kind at the AHA and for humanism generally to exempt those who see AI use as flying in the face of their freedom of conscience,” AHA staff attorney Alexandria Huiskens said to RNS . She also added, “For us, humanism is a comprehensive way of life. It’s built on inherent worth and dignity, and everyone should have room to exercise this comprehensive way of life at work the same way Christians do, or Muslims do.”

It should be noted that while anyone can request a Title VII exemption, it will only be granted if the applicant has a deep moral conviction that could count as an article of faith. Aside from that, the law also states that the request should not place an “undue hardship on the employer’s business.” So, even though Durman is no longer personally required to use AI tools for his tasks, he is still expected to attend meetings and cooperate with colleagues who use AI or to submit materials to AI tools, as needed.

AI use in corporate settings has been one of the biggest questions ever since LLMs exploded in popularity with ChatGPT. While AI proponents have said that the technology would increase productivity multiple times, reports say that corporate America, except for Big Tech, is not seeing any financial returns . Even so, about half of all U.S. employees now use AI one way or another at work, even as many executives remain uncertain about AI’s return on investment . But as for Durman, he says that the fact that Americans are already thinking about the impact of AI is a good thing, and that he hopes that his story would help others who’d rather not be forced to use the technology.

items.title: At A Worker-Run Game Studio, Employees Voted To Lose Their Jobs - Aftermath (Riley MacLeod)
items.content:
In early September, Montreal game studio KO-OP announced it would be “saying goodbye” to 13 people, citing–like so many others–difficulty finding funding. But unlike other layoffs in the games industry, which tend to strike suddenly from on-high, those affected had been involved in the decision from the beginning, and had actively voted for the outcome.

“As with all our company's operational decisions, this one was made democratically,” KO-OP wrote in its announcement. “Our members are regularly updated on our cash flow situation, and were made aware of this upcoming shortfall well in advance. Membership then appointed a group to plan for this eventuality, and ratified their recommendations. Team leads and our elected executives will also be impacted by these reductions. We believe this level of transparency and accountability ought to be a minimum requirement for all organizations.”

— KO_OP: 🪐 Wishlist Young Suns on Steam! ( @ko-op.com ) September 10, 2026 at 11:32 AM

It’s an unusual process for any company, but not necessarily one for KO-OP : The studio–which was founded in 2012, and has made games including Gnog, Goodbye Volcano High, and its current project Young Suns –operates as a co-operative. Everyone at the studio, which was roughly 30 people prior to the cuts, makes the same amount of money, $90K CAD ($63K USD). In addition to members’ game development work, they’re required to help with administrative tasks by joining committees dedicated to topics like hiring and finance, and membership meets every other month to talk as a group about how things are going and to vote on proposals about the studio.

“We try to call ourselves ‘worker run,’ because all of our operations are democratically operated and managed,” co-founder and studio director Saleem Dabbous told Aftermath over a video call, noting that the studio is still working toward legally becoming a co-op.

As the studio has grown, especially during production of Young Suns , its structure and operations have had to grow with it. Prior to the cuts, membership had elected a six-person “executive committee,” and it was this committee that was tasked with coming up with proposals for how to deal with KO-OP’s financial problems and, ultimately, who to let go.

Dabbous and former narrative designer Jenna Yow, who lost their job, largely referred to the cuts as furloughs, since KO-OP hopes to hire affected workers back. Affected workers are still eligible to receive any profits from Young Suns , and they can still attend studio meetings and vote on company decisions. They “still have the ability and the choice to be involved with the operations of the co-op at large, because it's in their best interest to see how things are progressing in case we're able to rehire them,” said Dabbous.

“With [a] layoff, generally, it's like a handshake, like a goodbye, it's done… Our intent is essentially to try to do the best we can by everybody, within our means, and to try to keep that as transparent as possible.”

And while workers didn’t know ahead of time who would be affected, they knew the cuts were coming and had time to prepare. This proved valuable for Yow, who was hired four and half years ago to work on narrative for Goodbye Volcano High as their first full-time job in the games industry out of college. During the furlough discussions, they had been trying to move to KO-OP’s Montreal office from the Seattle area. Aware they might not have a job and subsequently a visa if they moved, they were able to instead plan a move to live near family on the East Coast.

“Really the biggest benefit of it [was] just having the time to prepare… and then just kind of make plans accordingly, which is not something a lot of other people at other studios get to do,” Yow told Aftermath in the video call.

“Even though this situation is not one I would wish on anybody, I do feel like it's probably the best way it could have happened for anyone.”

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

items.title: H.264 Is Magic (2016)
items.content:
H.264 is a video compression codec standard. It is ubiquitous - internet video, Blu-ray, phones, security cameras, drones, everything. Everything uses H.264 now.

H.264 is a remarkable piece of technology. It is the result of 30+ years of work with one single goal: To reduce the bandwidth required for transmission of full-motion video.

Technically, it is very interesting. This post will give insight into some of the details at a high level - I hope to not bore you too much with the intricacies. Also note that many of the concepts explained here apply to video compression in general, and not just H.264.

A simple uncompressed video file will contain an array of 2D buffers containing pixel data for each frame. So it's a 3D (2 spatial dimensions and 1 temporal) array of bytes. Each pixel takes 3 bytes to store - one byte each for the three primary colors (red, green and blue).

1080p @ 60 Hz = 1920x1080x60x3 => ~ 370 MB/sec of raw data.

This is next to impossible to deal with. A 50GB Blu-ray disk will only hold ~2 mins. You can't move it anywhere fast. Even SSDs have trouble dumping this straight from RAM to Disk[^1].

Yes, I will answer this. But first let me show you something. Here is the Apple Homepage:

I captured the screen of this home page and produced two files:

PNG screenshot of the Apple homepage 1015KB

5 Second 60fps H.264 video of the same Apple homepage 175KB

Eh. What? Those file sizes look switched.

No, they're right. The H.264 video, 300 frames long is 175KB. A single frame of that video in PNG is 1015KB.

It looks like we're storing 300 times the amount of data in the video. But the file size is a fifth. So H.264 would seem to be 1500x as efficient as PNG.

How is this even possible? All right, what's the trick?

There are very many tricks! H.264 uses all the tricks you can think of (and tons you can't think of). Let's go through the important ones.

Imagine you're building a car for street racing. You need to go faster. What is the first thing you do? You shed some weight. Your car weighs 3000 lbs. You throw away stuff you don't need. Those back seats? pfft. Chuck those. That subwoofer? Gone. No music for you. Air Conditioning? Yeah, ditch it. Transmission? Ye..no. Wait! We're gonna need that.

You remove everything except the things that matter.

This concept of throwing away bits you don't need to save space is called lossy compression. H.264 is a lossy codec - it throws away less important bits and only keeps the important bits.

PNG is a lossless codec. It means that nothing is thrown away. Bit for bit, the original source image can be recovered from a PNG encoded image.

Important bits? How does the algorithm know what bits in my frame are important?

There are few obvious ways to trim out images. Maybe the top right quadrant is useless all the time. So maybe we can zero out those pixels and discard that quadrant. We would use only 3/4th of the space we need. ~2200 lbs now. Or maybe we can crop out a thick border around the edges of the frame, the important stuff is in the middle anyway. Yes, you could do these. But H.264 doesn't do this.

H.264, like other lossy image algorithms, discards detail information. Here is a close-up of the original compared with the image post-discard.

See how the compressed one does not show the holes in the speaker grills in the MacBook Pro? If you don't zoom in, you would even notice the difference. The image on the right weighs in at 7% the size of the original - and we haven't even compressed the image in the traditional sense. Imagine your car weighed just 200 lbs!

7% wow! How do you discard detail information like that?

Now we're getting to the juicy bits! Ha puns! If you took an information theory class, you might remember information entropy. Information entropy is the number of bits required to represent some information. Note that it is not simply the size of some dataset. It is minimum number of bits that must be used to represent all the information…

items.title: HP Poly VoIP vulnerability sets the stage for executive voice deepfakes
items.content:
HP has released patches for a critical buffer overflow vulnerability in multiple IP-enabled conference phones from its Poly Voice line. The flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain root privileges on the underlying operating system, potentially enabling them to execute other attacks such as eavesdropping on conversations and recording voice data for AI-enabled impersonation attacks.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-0826 , was discovered by researchers from security firm Rapid7 and resides in the code that parses Session Description Protocol (SDP) attributes when the Interactive Connectivity Establishment (ICE) feature is enabled.

ICE enables VoIP devices to establish peer-to-peer connections using the shortest available network path. The feature is not enabled by default on HP Poly devices, and the company advises administrators to disable it if it’s not needed.

The flaw, rated 9.2 on the CVSS severity scale, affects all phones from the HP Poly VVX series, as well as the Trio 8300, 8500, and 8800 IP conference devices. HP has fixed the flaw in its Poly Unified Communications Software (UCS) versions 6.4.8 for the VVX devices, 8.1.7 for the Trio 8300, and 7.2.8 for Trio 8500 and 8800.

An exploit module targeting this vulnerability has already been developed and released for the widely used Metasploit penetration testing framework that’s maintained by Rapid7.

The exploit executes code as root on an affected device with ICE enabled by sending a SIP INVITE request with a specially crafted candidate attribute. This attribute normally contains a transport address that can be used for connectivity checks and is part of the ICE RFC8839 standard.

The buffer overflow bug is located in a helper function called ParseICECandidate in the polyapp binary that processes such requests on the device.

“The start of the function contains a call to memcpy , which will copy the incoming string line being processed into a 256 byte stack buffer,” Stephen Fewer, senior principal security researcher at Rapid7, said in a blog post . “No length check is performed to ensure the incoming string length is less than 256 bytes. Therefore by providing a candidate attribute whose length is greater than 256 bytes, a stack-based buffer overflow will occur.”

Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR), a kernel feature that randomizes memory addresses to defeat buffer overflow exploits, is enabled on the device. However, the protection is not operating correctly on the HP Poly devices because it does not randomize the load addresses of .so (Shared Object) libraries.

These libraries, such as libc , are loaded by other processes, including the polyapp process, and because their memory addresses never change, they can be leveraged to bypass ASLR and execute the attacker’s payload.

“We create a ROP chain that will execute an arbitrary OS command via the system standard C library function,” Fewer said. “The accompanying Metasploit exploit modules source code details the entire ROP chain.”

Attackers have increasingly targeted embedded devices inside enterprise networks in recent years because unlike laptops, workstations, and servers, these devices are not monitored by endpoint detection and response (EDR) products. As such, they provide perfect footholds inside corporate environments that allow attackers to remain undetected for long periods of time and attack other systems.

In the age of AI these devices become even more relevant for attackers, going beyond corporate espionage by recording conversations or internal network pivoting.

“Attackers no longer need massive datasets to make use of synthetic speech tooling,” Douglas McKee, Rapid7’s director of vulnerability intelligence, said in a blog post . “In many cases, they just need clean source audio of the right person saying enough words in enough contexts. That has made executive voice data, call recordings, and live conversation capture far more valuable than many organizations seem prepared…
